key_insight: JEV matched Qwen Flash’s batch-mode macro-F1 on two datasets and outperformed it on MIMIC-III, with lower observed latency and estimated cost.
clinical_relevance: JEV could support trial prescreening by assessing individual criteria and flagging information gaps for human review.
method: Retrospectively evaluated 2,048 patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and MIMIC-III/IV-derived question-answer datasets.
Compared non-generative JEV with schema-constrained Qwen Flash in individual and shared-context batch modes.
Measured performance against reference labels under strict Zero Data Retention policies.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-III in batch mode, JEV achieved macro-F1 of 0.768 versus 0.534 (difference: +0.234; 95% CI: 0.187–0.281), with higher recall for insufficient-information labels (56.3% versus 9.9%).
watch_item: This retrospective evaluation does not establish clinical readiness; evidence-interpretation errors require verification against patient records before eligibility decisions.
paper_title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
